section_entries.label: Periodic-orbit survival and Mellin representation
section_entries.mathematical_role: Identifies near-periodic trajectories as the long-time survivors, integrates their phase-space neighborhoods, compresses the orbit sum with the Ramanujan identity, and introduces Mellin inversion for small-hole asymptotics.

section_entries.label: Rational separation and character reduction
section_entries.mathematical_role: Splits orbit periods into residue classes, uses Dirichlet-character orthogonality and Euler products, and obtains the rational two-hole Mellin integrand in terms of L-functions.

unit_result_entry.title: Rational hole separation becomes residue-class harmonic analysis
unit_result_entry.why_material: For rational theta, the orbit-period sum splits by congruence classes modulo q; dividing by the class gcd produces coprime reduced data, and Dirichlet-character orthogonality acts as the projector selecting a residue class.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The definitions of reduced a-prime and q-prime and the character convention that vanishes off the units modulo q-prime are part of the required setup.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the group and orthogonality prose is clear, but primes, congruences, and the displayed delta identity need scan verification because columns and symbols are interleaved.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Mellin inversion converts small-hole behavior into a residue problem
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The finite, piecewise-smooth long-time coefficient is Mellin transformed in hole width, the orbit sum is interchanged with the integral in a convergence half-plane, and inverse Mellin integration makes the small-hole expansion a sum of residues.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Euler products turn the congruence sum into Dirichlet L-function ratios
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Inserting character orthogonality permits a sum over all integers; prime factorization then separates the totient and Möbius contributions into Euler factors, yielding a character sum involving L(s,chi) over L(s+1,chi). The trivial character recovers zeta with factors at primes dividing the modulus removed.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Rational hole separation makes the fractional-part weights periodic in the orbit period. Splitting periods modulo q, reducing each class by its gcd with q, and applying Dirichlet-character orthogonality turns a congruence restriction into a finite harmonic projector.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For theta=2 pi r/q with gcd(r,q)=1, the required period sum splits into classes n congruent to a modulo q. With b=gcd(a,q), the source sets n'=n/b, a'=a/b, and q'=q/b, so a' is coprime to q'. Dirichlet characters modulo q' are extended by zero off the units, and their orthogonality relation represents the residue-class delta.
directed.conceptual_reading: The gcd reduction isolates the invertible residue data needed for group characters. Orthogonality then replaces a hard congruence constraint by a superposition of multiplicative modes that can be factored prime by prime.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Dirichlet characters are the bridge from additive residue-class selection to multiplicative harmonic analysis and ultimately to L-functions.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The finite character projector applies because theta is rational and the weights are residue-class data; it does not extend directly to irrational separation. Formula symbols and congruences are partially interleaved with a figure.
directed.uncertainty: The algebraic setup is clear in prose, though the exact normalization of the displayed orthogonality identity should be checked against the original page for symbolic reuse.

supported: For rational theta, the source splits the period sum into congruence classes modulo q.

It divides by b equal to gcd(a,q), obtains coprime reduced a-prime and q-prime, defines Dirichlet characters on the units extended by zero, and gives their orthogonality projector for the residue class.
inference: Describing orthogonality as replacing a hard congruence restriction by multiplicative modes is a faithful interpretation of the displayed projector.
unsupported_or_imported: Prime-by-prime factorization and the arrival at L-functions occur in the following derivation, not in this unit's evidence boundary.
The claim that Dirichlet characters ultimately bridge to L-functions therefore imports the next unit's conclusion.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Two cancellations isolate the zeta-sensitive remainder: subtract the leading 2/epsilon term from one-hole escape, or subtract twice the symmetric two-hole escape from the one-hole quantity. P_1 is the one-hole problem and P_2 the symmetric two-hole problem.
